title: Present Tense 6: Core Irregulars (хотеть, мочь, есть)
titleRussian: Настоящее время 6: ключевые исключения (хотеть, мочь, есть)
description: Three of the most-used Russian verbs do their own thing. Хотеть mixes both conjugations. Мочь alternates between two stems. Есть has its own tiny paradigm.
descriptionRussian: Три самых частотных глагола конъюгируются нестандартно: хотеть (смешанное спряжение), мочь (чередование основ мог / мож), есть (свой собственный набор окончаний).
intro: To want, to be able, to eat. Three verbs, and between them they will carry more of your early Russian than any rule in this book. They also break both systems you have just spent five lessons building, which feels like a betrayal and is actually a mercy: verbs this common get worn smooth by use, and irregular forms survive precisely because they are said too often to be forgotten. Pin each one to a sentence you genuinely want to say.
rules: Хотеть has mixed conjugation: singular uses 1st-conj endings (хочу́, хо́чешь, хо́чет), plural uses 2nd-conj endings (хоти́м, хоти́те, хотя́т). The stem alternates хоч- / хот- between singular and plural.
Мочь has stem alternation: мог- in 1sg and 3pl (могу́, мо́гут), мож- in the other four forms (мо́жешь, мо́жет, мо́жем, мо́жете). All endings are 1st-conjugation.

Есть has its own miniature paradigm. Singular: ем, ешь, ест (no thematic vowel). Plural: едим, едите, едят (2nd-conj endings on the stem ед-). The verb 'есть' meaning 'there is / has' (У меня есть собака) is a fixed form and does not conjugate.
These three verbs are among the top 50 most-frequent Russian verbs. Memorize the full paradigm of each rather than trying to derive it.
examples: Я хочу́ горячий чай. (I want hot tea.) Singular 1sg: 1st-conj ending -у́, husher rule on the stem хоч-.
Мы хоти́м поехать на море летом. (We want to go to the sea in the summer.) Plural 1pl: 2nd-conj ending -им, stem changes to хот-.
Они хотя́т пойти в кино. (They want to go to the movies.) Plural 3pl: 2nd-conj ending -ят on stem хот-.
Я могу́ помочь тебе с домашним заданием. (I can help you with your homework.) Стем мог-, end-stressed -у́.
Маша мо́жет говорить на трёх языках. (Masha can speak three languages.) Stem мож-, stem-stressed -ет.
Дети едя́т кашу на завтрак. Я ем хлеб с маслом. (The children eat porridge for breakfast. I eat bread with butter.) Plural 3pl: едят. Singular 1sg: ем.

items.prompt: Студенты громко _____ во дворе после уроков.
items.promptEnglish: The students are shouting loudly in the yard after class. (Which 3pl form has the correct ending?)
items.hint: Warm-up from Lesson 5. Subject is 3pl, stem ends in a husher. Which 3pl ending appears after a husher?
items.explanation: Recall from Lesson 5: студенты is 3pl. Кричать has stem крич- ending in the husher -ч-. The Russian spelling rule blocks я after a husher, so the 3pl ending switches from -ят to -ат: кричат.

items.promptEnglish: I want hot tea with lemon. (Which 1sg form is correctly built?)
items.hint: Хотеть has mixed conjugation AND a stem alternation. Which stem appears in the singular?
items.explanation: Хотеть alternates its stem: хоч- in the singular, хот- in the plural. The 1sg uses 1st-conj -у on the singular stem хоч-, giving хочу.

items.prompt: Мы _____ поехать на море этим летом.
items.promptEnglish: We want to travel to the sea this summer. (Which 1pl form is correctly built?)
items.hint: Plural хотеть switches BOTH the stem (хоч- → хот-) AND the conjugation class (1st → 2nd). Apply both.
items.explanation: Хотеть's plurals switch stem (хоч- → хот-) and conjugation class (1st → 2nd). 1pl: stem хот- + 2nd-conj -им = хотим.

items.prompt: Я _____ помочь тебе с домашним заданием.
items.promptEnglish: I can help you with your homework. (Which 1sg form uses the correct stem?)
items.hint: Я + мочь. Mostly the verb uses stem мож-. Which two slots break that and use стем мог-?
items.explanation: Мочь alternates between two stems: мог- in only the 1sg and 3pl (могу, могут), and мож- in the other four forms (можешь, может, можем, можете). The 1sg is могу.

items.promptEnglish: Masha can speak three languages. (Which 3sg form uses the correct stem?)
items.hint: Маша is 3sg. 3sg is NOT one of the мог- slots. Which stem belongs here?
items.explanation: Маша is 3sg. The 3sg of мочь uses stem мож- with the 1st-conj ending -ет: может. Only the 1sg and 3pl use the stem мог-.

items.prompt: Мы _____ кашу на завтрак каждое утро.
items.promptEnglish: We eat porridge for breakfast every morning. (Which 1pl form uses the correct stem?)
items.hint: Есть splits its paradigm: bare stem in the singular, but a different stem in the plural. Which stem appears in the 1pl?
items.explanation: Есть's singular uses no theme vowel (ем / ешь / ест), but the plural switches to the stem ед- with 2nd-conj endings: едим / едите / едят.

blanks: Дети _____ суп с большим аппетитом. (The children are eating soup with great appetite.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Subject дети is 3pl. The 3pl form of есть is едят: plural stem ед- plus 2nd-conj ending -ят.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton wants a big cup of coffee.
errorCorrection.explanation: Хотеть alternates its stem: хоч- in the singular, хот- in the plural. The 3sg uses the singular stem with the 1st-conjugation ending: хочет. Хотит mixes the plural stem хот- with a 2nd-conjugation ending; neither belongs in the 3sg slot.

Мочь alternates between two stems: мог- appears only in the 1sg and 3pl (могу, могут), while мож- appears in the other four forms. The 3pl is могут. Можут wrongly extends the мож- stem into one of the two мог- slots.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The guests are eating cake in the kitchen.
errorCorrection.explanation: Есть splits its paradigm: the singular uses no theme vowel (ем, ешь, ест), but the plural switches to the stem ед- with second-conjugation endings (едим, едите, едят). The 3pl is едят. Естят wrongly extends the singular's ест- stem into the plural.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha wants coffee with milk in the morning. (Both options are 3sg; pick the one with the right stem.)
minimalPairs.explanation: Хотеть's singulars use stem хоч-: хочет. Хотет wrongly keeps the infinitive's хот- stem.

minimalPairs.context: Мои дети _____ играть на улице после школы.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: My children can play outside after school. (Both options are 3pl; pick the one with the right stem.)
minimalPairs.explanation: Мочь's 3pl is one of the two slots that use stem мог-: могут. Можут wrongly keeps the мож- stem.

reviewVocab.definition: mixed conjugation (a paradigm that combines 1st-conj endings in some slots with 2nd-conj endings in others; the only common modern Russian example is хотеть)
reviewVocab.example: У глагола 'хотеть' смешанное спряжение: хочу́, хо́чешь, хо́чет — первое спряжение; хоти́м, хоти́те, хотя́т — второе.

reviewVocab.definition: stem alternation (the appearance of two different stems across one verb's paradigm; in мочь the stems are мог- and мож-)
reviewVocab.example: В глаголе 'мочь' чередование основ мог- и мож-: я могу́, ты мо́жешь, они мо́гут.

reviewVocab.definition: exception (a verb whose forms are not fully predictable from either standard conjugation; must be memorized)
reviewVocab.example: Глаголы 'хотеть', 'мочь' и 'есть' — самые частотные исключения в русском языке.
